done_when: Every pytest command in .github/workflows/forge-next.yml and forge.yml passes -o faulthandler_timeout=120, so a test still running after two minutes prints every thread's stack to the job log before the cap cancels it; no new dependency

findings.body: `forge.toml:5` still defines the test command without the timeout. `src/forge/sync.py:223–226` inserts that command into this workflow, and lines 255–263 overwrite differing files. Consequently, the next `forge sync` removes the timeout and makes the new regression test fail. This also immediately triggers the workflow-drift diagnostics in `src/forge/doctor.py:98–99,133–135`. Add the timeout to `forge.toml` so regeneration preserves the fix.
findings.title: Preserve the timeout in the generated workflow's source configuration

why: When a test hangs on CI the job is cancelled at its time cap and GitHub keeps no log, so nobody can tell which test hung (Windows group 1 hung for 10 minutes on PR 294)
